# Supported games

The modding guides are written for every game. Each game's facts live in two places: the generated identity
block below, and the game's own guide, which covers its install options, worked-example values and quirks.
Use the game id wherever a guide writes `<game>`.

A game has two support levels, which its profile manifest states (`support`). Play says how well the engine
runs it: P1 recognized (the engine reads all of it, and nothing runs), P2 boots, P3 complete (every opcode
its scripts use is handled, and it saves), P4 verified against the original to its ending. Modding says
what a modder gets: M1 scripts, M2 documented data, M3 a base mod. A game is supported at P3 and M3; one
below P3 is still being added and is not playable. The levels' gates are in
[Adding a game](../../adding-a-game.md).

| Game | Id | Engine ABI | Play | Modding | Guide |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Soukoku no Arterial | `arterial` | `SYS4438` | P3 (complete) | M3 (base mod) | [the guide](arterial.md) |
| Ikusa Megami ZERO | `bg0` | `SYS4415` | P2 (boots) | none | none yet |
| Himegari Dungeon Meister | `himegari` | `SYS4422` | P3 (complete) | M3 (base mod) | [the guide](himegari.md) |
| Kamidori Alchemy Meister | `kamidori` | `SYS4433` | P3 (complete) | M3 (base mod) | [the guide](kamidori.md) |

## Adding a game

A new profile manifest (`engine/Ome.Engine/Profiles/<id>.json`) adds a row and an identity block here when
this page is regenerated. Write its guide as `games/<id>.md`, following the existing ones, and keep game
facts out of the generic guides.
